trustPolicyPublished: {tag} was published only after clearing that path: a build that fails signing or notarization verification never becomes a release asset.

archHelpBody: Open the Apple menu in the top-left corner and choose About This Mac. If "Chip" begins with Apple M, you have Apple Silicon; if "Processor" says Intel, you have Intel.
demoHeading: People and agents reading the same meaning
heroLead: Give Claude Code or Codex task context over MCP from one shared Markdown vault. Inspect recorded capabilities and rules, their evidence, and what remains unknown. Decide which proposed meaning changes to keep.
closingVerifyBody: Run this in a terminal once the download finishes. The hash it prints must match the one below; if it does not, the file is not the one we published.
demoTitle: Inspect the context your agent reads
demoSub: This recorded demo selects a concept and its evidence, then Codex follows a declared path in the same vault. It shows a bounded lookup, not a complete change-impact check.
demoPromptLabel: What Codex was asked in this take
demoAgentPrompt: Use only `get_concept` and `find_path` to explain the path from `capabilities/mcp-tool-server` to `capabilities/ontology-map` in one sentence. Do not change files.
demoProvisionalNote: {seconds}s from one take. Only the agent's thinking time is cut; nothing is sped up, and there is no sound.
evidenceTitle: Meaning you can inspect, in files you own
evidenceSub: The map reads this repository’s Markdown vault. Beside it is an actual file: the recorded capability, its declared relationship, and the implementation path an agent can inspect.
specimenElided: These {shown} lines become one node and one line on the map. The other {count} (ids and bookkeeping) are not shown.
specimenComplete: These {shown} lines become one node and one line on the map.
specimenFooter: There are <n>{count}</n> files like this, and every line on the map comes from them.
agentsTitle: Give your agent context. Keep meaning reviewable.
agentsSub: Atlas finds Claude Agent and Codex on this computer, and either one can work in the app's own chat. Reads go straight through; every Atlas write waits until you allow it once. No Atlas account and no new API key.
acpSceneTab: In-app chat · a write waits for you
acpUserMsg: The payment feature leans on user auth; if auth goes down, payments go down with it
acpToolCaption: The agent's Atlas write request · review required before it runs
acpToolWhy: user note: the payment feature leans on user auth, so if auth goes down payments go down with it (2026-08-16)
acpResultLine: ✓ Approved once · one relation written into a markdown file in your folder
col1Body: Claude Agent and Codex both run in the in-app chat. Codex opens in its read-only mode, and a file it changes inside the folder shows up in Git, where you can undo it. Atlas starts the local adapter and its agent connection server (MCP); the agent itself may still talk to its own provider.
col1Code: Agent connector · runs on your machine
col2Title: Review the proposed meaning before it is written
col2Body: In the in-app Atlas ontology-write flow shown here, reads proceed and writes pause for exact review. External MCP clients apply their own permissions; meaning acceptance is separate from code approval.
col2Code: Atlas read → allow · Atlas write → review
col3Title: Keep context for the next task
col3Body: The same Markdown remains on your disk for people and agents to read, correct, and reuse. No Atlas account or backend.
